column1: # Golden envelopes every runtime must reproduce byte for byte.
# One case per line. Fields are tab separated `key=value` pairs, so all three
# languages can read them without a JSON parser -- the Rust crate stays
# dependency-free -- and an optional field is simply absent rather than an empty
# column somebody has to count. Only the first `=` separates; values may contain
# more, which is why `expected` can be JSON.
# Keys: name, failure_point, code, service, impact, detail,
#       cause_failure_point, cause_code, cause_service, cause_impact,
#       cause_detail, context, expected
# The cases are real: every one is a failure this fleet produced while the
# vocabulary lived in six copies and the gateway had none.
name=credential-refused
column6: detail=provider_authentication: OAuth access token has been revoked.
column7: expected={"failure_point":"brama.dispatch.bounded-rotation","error_code":"auth","service":"brama","impact":"one model request","severity":"warning","retryable":false,"outage":false,"detail":"provider_authentication: OAuth access token has been revoked."}

column1: # A call site that knows its code exactly and has no layer below to quote.
# growth-tactics reaches this: classify_failure("accounts.job", code=NOT_FOUND).
name=quiet-refusal
# One segment. stado's failure points come from the clap subcommand path and
# `cli` is one of them; a rule that refused it was the package being wrong.
name=single-segment
# Four segments, from a nested subcommand: the depth carries no meaning.
name=deep-segment
# The builder that must never throw, on the two violations all three runtimes can
# express. An off-catalogue code is deliberately absent from this case: in Rust it
# cannot be handed one, because Code is an enum and the type system refuses it
# before a note could be recorded. JS and Python agree byte for byte on that path
# too; it just has no Rust side to compare against.
name=salvaged-malformed
